summary: Feed s172_triple is degraded: 100% of packets missing required VLANs 10,20, 13.30 Gbps microbursts overload 10 Gbps APM port (133%), and 27.9% ERSPAN tunnel traffic obscures inner flows.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker or TAP/SPAN is stripping 802.1Q tags - 100% of packets arrive untagged despite APM requiring VLANs 10 and 20 for tier/tenant segmentation. Likely broker VLAN stripping / pop-tag policy or SPAN from access ports without trunk preservation.
findings.impact_on_tool: APM cannot filter, group, or baseline by application tier/VLAN; transactions from VLAN 10 and 20 are merged, breaking service maps, latency baselines, and alerting by business unit.

recommended_fix.why: Restore and preserve 802.1Q tags end-to-end so APM receives VLAN 10,20 classification needed for correct APM segmentation.

findings.root_cause: Aggregate/burst throughput exceeds APM port capacity - 13.30 Gbps peak in 1ms burst vs 10 Gbps port (133% load, 2 overloaded intervals). Single 10G tool port fed without load-balancing or burst shaping from broker.
findings.impact_on_tool: APM NIC drops packets during microbursts causing incomplete transactions, false latency/loss calculations, missed traces and degraded application performance visibility.

recommended_fix.why: Distribute traffic across 2x10G APM ports with flow-aware hashing to keep per-port load <80% and eliminate burst drops while preserving flow coherence for APM.

findings.root_cause: 27.9% of frames (2310/8286) arrive encapsulated in ERSPAN and are not stripped by packet broker. APM receives outer tunnel headers instead of inner application traffic.
findings.impact_on_tool: APM cannot parse inner L4-L7 headers, fails to decode transactions and measure true application latency; tunnel overhead inflates metrics and hides real endpoints.

recommended_fix.why: Terminate/strip ERSPAN at the packet broker to deliver native inner packets so APM can correctly dissect flows and compute application performance.
